# GEO report: harbor-site

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 40/100, At risk

Confidence: High (checked 25 of 25 points).
How it's calculated: low = 16.33 ÷ 25 × 100 = 65. High = (16.33 + 0) ÷ 25 × 100 = 65. The cap then applies: a search crawler is blocked site-wide (GEO-009), so neither number can be above 40.

Everything was readable from code, so there are no unknowns. The cap comes from `robots.txt` blocking two AI search crawlers. Without the cap the arithmetic gives 65. I sampled all 3 routes: `/`, `/moorings` and `/contact`.

## Live check

- **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

### 1. Let the AI search crawlers in (or confirm that blocking them is intended)
- **Why it matters:** `OAI-SearchBot` (ChatGPT search) and `PerplexityBot` are blocked from the whole site. Those tools can't read the pages, so they have no source to quote.
- **Where:** `public/robots.txt:4-8`
- **What the code says:** `User-agent: OAI-SearchBot` / `Disallow: /` (and the same for `PerplexityBot`)
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 77 (the cap lifts and GEO-009 earns its full 3 points). I assumed you want to be found, because there is no `geo.config.json`. If the block is deliberate, tell me and I'll treat it as a declared policy.

### 2. Fix the two broken FAQ and Article structured data blocks
- **Why it matters:** JSON-LD is machine-readable markup that labels page facts. Both blocks here are broken, so they are invalid or incomplete and tools can't use them.
- **Where:** `src/data/faq.json:8` and `src/pages/moorings.astro:9`
- **What the code says:** `" ": {` (the key should be `acceptedAnswer`). On the Article, `"headline": "Moorings and prices", }` has a trailing comma, so the JSON is invalid.
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 40 on its own, because the cap from item 1 is still in force. With items 1 and 2 together it is 85.

### 3. Give each page its own canonical URL
- **Why it matters:** A canonical tells search engines which address is the official one for a page. Every page currently says the official address is the home page. That can lead engines to drop `/moorings` and `/contact` in favour of `/`.
- **Where:** `src/layouts/Base.astro:8`
- **What the code says:** `<link rel="canonical" href="https://harbor.example/" />`
- **Size:** Small. Build the URL from `Astro.url.pathname`, or pass a `canonical` prop from each page, joined to `https://harbor.example`.
- **Score after this:** 40 on its own. With items 1 and 3 it is 83. With all three items it is 91.

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid | Clear | `public/robots.txt`, valid lines, tiny file |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers have access | Problem | `public/robots.txt:4-8` (0 of 3 points, blocker, cap 40) |
| GEO-014 | Routes are indexable | Problem | `src/pages/contact.astro:4` has `robots="noindex"`, yet `/contact` is in the sitemap and the nav (2 of 3 routes clear) |
| GEO-015 | Absolute canonical per page | Problem | `src/layouts/Base.astro:8` (1 of 3 routes clear) |
| GEO-003 | Content in server HTML | Clear | Astro renders static HTML; text is in the `.astro` pages |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Problem | `src/data/faq.json:8`, `src/pages/moorings.astro:9` (both JSON-LD routes fail) |
| GEO-011 | Sitemap discoverable | Clear | `public/sitemap.xml`, `Sitemap:` line at `robots.txt:10` |
| GEO-012 | Title, description, lang | Clear | `Base.astro:4-7`; all 3 pages pass non-empty values |
| GEO-016 | Links are crawlable | Clear | `Base.astro:12`, plain `<a href>` |
| GEO-017 | Snippet limits vs AI policy | Problem | `Base.astro:9` (2 of 3 routes affected) |
| GEO-002 | Accessibility basics | Clear | Read `Newsletter.jsx` and `Base.astro`: no images, labelled input, text button |
| GEO-101 | App association files | Not applicable | No mobile app declared |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt (info only) | Not applicable | Not present; not scored |
| GEO-102 | App structured data (info only) | Not applicable | Not scored |

## Other problems found

- **Noindexed page listed in the sitemap:** `public/sitemap.xml:5`: `<loc>https://harbor.example/contact</loc>`, while `src/pages/contact.astro:4` sets `robots="noindex"`. Either remove it from the sitemap or drop the noindex.
- **Default hides page text from snippets:** `src/layouts/Base.astro:9`: `content={robots ?? "max-snippet:0"}`. The fallback applies `max-snippet:0` to every page that doesn't set `robots`, which stops search and AI tools quoting text from the page. Use `index, follow` as the default.

## Worth considering

- **Label the business with structured data:** `src/pages/contact.astro:6`: `Call the harbour office on 01326 000000.` Adding `LocalBusiness` or `Organization` JSON-LD with the name and phone number might help machines identify who runs the site. Add the address as well.
- **Back the price claim with detail:** `src/pages/moorings.astro:7`: `Prices start at £40 a night.` The page promises "Mooring sizes and seasonal prices" (line 5) but gives only one number. Add a table of sizes and seasonal rates as real text.
- **Answer the FAQ in visible text:** `src/pages/index.astro:8`. The night-booking and water-taxi answers appear only in JSON-LD. Show the same Q&A on the page so visitors can read it too.
- **Add dates to the sitemap:** `public/sitemap.xml:3-5`: `<url><loc>…</loc></url>` has no `<lastmod>`. Add dates if you know when each page last changed.
- **Generate the sitemap:** `package.json:9` has no `@astrojs/sitemap`. Set `site: "https://harbor.example"` in `astro.config` (there is no config file). The framework can then build the sitemap and canonicals for you.
- **Add head basics:** `src/layouts/Base.astro:5-10` sets no `charset`, `viewport` or Open Graph tags (`og:title` and similar). Add them.
- **Add page structure:** `Base.astro:13` has no `<main>` around `<slot />`. Wrapping it helps tools find the primary content.
- **Make the home page more specific:** `src/pages/index.astro:5`: `description="Book a mooring in Falmouth harbour."` The title says "Harbor" and "Cornwall" and the heading says "Falmouth". Choose one spelling and say who the harbour office is.
- **Link the pages together:** `index.astro:7` mentions moorings and a water taxi but has no link to `/moorings` or `/contact` in the body text. Add inline links.

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs <access log>`, which checks real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **Server answers:** the live status codes for `/robots.txt`, the sitemap URLs and any `X-Robots-Tag` headers are set at hosting, not in this repo. A live scan with your URL would confirm them.

## Assumptions

- You want search engines and AI search tools to find this site, because there is no `geo.config.json`. If the `OAI-SearchBot` and `PerplexityBot` blocks are on purpose, GEO-009 and GEO-017 change.
- `https://harbor.example` is the site's real origin, as declared in the sitemap and `robots.txt`.
- Blocking training crawlers such as `GPTBot` or `ClaudeBot` isn't present here, so nothing to note on that.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
